name: Barrett Plastics
old_description: Barrett Plastics, LLC. is a plastic injection molding company located in northwest Arkansas, USA, where we specialize in both proprietary and custom molding.
about:
Barrett Plastics, LLC operates from Harrison, Arkansas, in the northwest corner of the state. The company was founded in 2024 and focuses on plastic injection molding for both proprietary product lines and custom orders. (No founders or ownership details disclosed.)

The shop runs injection molding machines ranging from 101 to 528 tons, supported by an in-house design, fabrication, and mold shop. A vertical CNC milling center complements the tooling capabilities. Finished goods are stored in an on-site warehouse and a larger off-site facility, enabling just-in-time delivery programs. The company’s proprietary product line includes a range of caps and plungers such as Fez Caps, Stand Up Caps, Flat Caps, Snap-On Caps, Lube Caps, Reverse-Taper Caps, Flat Top Piercer Caps, Grease Tip Caps, and Cartridge Plungers.

Barrett Plastics serves customers needing custom-molded plastic components, particularly in the cap and closure segment. The company does not publicly list specific industry verticals, but its product portfolio suggests applications in packaging, fluid handling, and consumer goods.

The company emphasizes precision, quality, and competitive pricing, with a stated commitment to improving business practices and expanding its customer base. ISO 9001 certification underscores its quality management system.

name: Barth Electronics
old_description: Please contact Barth Electronics, Inc. for general company inquiries and technical information on Pulse Power products or ESD test equipment. Complete our contact form with your information, requests and feedback.
about:
Barth Electronics, Inc. has operated from Boulder City, Nevada since 1976, after originating in Ohio in 1964. The company was founded to design and manufacture specialized test hardware for weapons programs at the Nevada Test Site, serving clients such as EG&G and national laboratories.

Today the firm designs and manufactures sub‑nanosecond, high‑energy pulse power instrumentation and electrostatic discharge (ESD) test equipment. Its product line includes more than 100 pulse power items — among them the Model 4002 TLP+ for Human Body Model testing, the Model 4012 VFTLP+ for Charged Device Model testing, and the Model 4702 HMM+ for IEC‑equivalent gun discharge voltage testing. The company also runs a rental program for the Model 4002 TLP+ and offers complete ESD device testing services performed entirely at its Boulder City factory.

Customers span the semiconductor industry, physics and pulse‑power research laboratories, and government research facilities. Early work for EG&G and the national laboratories established a base in high‑reliability measurement; that heritage now supports commercial IC qualification and device characterization.

The company traces its commercial ESD line to a 1997 breakthrough — the first commercial Transmission Line Pulser — which adapted weapons‑test hardware for semiconductor reliability. Management says the high‑reliability culture from defense programs carries over into every instrument, and that ongoing R&D targets emerging ESD and high‑voltage pulse‑power needs.

name: Base Power Company
old_description: Base Power is an Austin, Texas-based company that designs, assembles, and deploys home battery backup systems while operating as a retail electric provider in Texas.
about:
Base Power Company is headquartered in Austin, Texas, and was founded in 2023 by CEO Zach Dell and co‑founder Justin Lopas. Dell, a Texas native, was motivated by Winter Storm Uri’s widespread outages, while Lopas brought manufacturing experience from SpaceX and Anduril. The pair assembled a team with backgrounds in satellite constellations and early‑scale electric‑vehicle production to address rising electricity costs and grid reliability.

The company designs, assembles, and deploys its own 39.2 kWh whole‑home battery system — called Core — and operates as a retail electric provider in Texas and Illinois. Its in‑house capabilities include battery pack assembly, UL‑certified testing, and virtual‑power‑plant grid‑services operation. As of the latest public figures, more than 30,000 homes have been equipped with Base hardware, which is rated for –22 °F to 122 °F, flash flooding, and submersion up to three feet.

Base serves residential homeowners across Texas and Illinois, with a concentration in Oncor territory, and positions its grid‑balancing battery network as a resource for utilities and grid operators. Customer testimonials cite installations in Waxahachie, Cypress, Houston, Arlington, Saginaw, and Pflugerville, and the company counts former NFL player JJ Watt as both an investor and a member.

The founders state they started Base to make electricity affordable and reliable again, offering automatic whole‑home backup at a fraction of traditional generator cost and earning revenue from grid services rather than markup on energy. The goal is to become the first power company customers genuinely love.

about:
Basic American Foods is headquartered in Idaho Falls, Idaho. The company was founded in 1933 by Jack Hume as a modest dehydration plant in California before establishing its current headquarters in Idaho Falls. It remains a privately held business.

The company manufactures dehydrated and prepared food products for both foodservice and retail channels. Its portfolio includes shelf-stable and refrigerated items designed for ease of preparation and consistent quality, serving high-volume kitchens and store shelves alike. Specific production processes, facility size, and output volumes are not publicly disclosed.

Basic American Foods supplies restaurants, schools, hospitals, grocery stores, and club stores worldwide. Its customer base spans the foodservice sector — including institutional dining — and the retail sector, where its brands appear on grocery and club-store shelves.

The company traces its differentiation to its founding principles of integrity and taste, aiming to help people serve great food to as many people as possible. Its stated mission is to make "real food heroes every day by providing customers with foods that are delicious to eat, easy to prepare and accessible to all."

about:
Battlefield Fabrication operates from Searcy, Arkansas, where it runs a family-owned construction and building-supply business. The company does not disclose its founding year or the names of its founders, but it describes itself as a small, family-owned operation that has grown into a licensed and insured contractor serving White County and the surrounding Central Arkansas region.

The company provides a full range of site-to-finish services: site preparation and dirt work (clearing, grading), concrete foundations (slabs and footings), and custom construction of barndominiums, pole barns, stud-wall shops, and portable buildings. It also installs standing-seam and exposed-fastener metal roofing, supplies building kits (shop kits and portable-building kits), and offers LVP flooring and countertop installation. The firm operates from a location at 2910 Highway 16 in Searcy, but it does not publish facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures.

Battlefield Fabrication serves property owners and developers in White County and nearby areas who need agricultural structures such as pole barns, residential barndominiums, commercial shop buildings, and portable storage or office units. The company markets itself as a turnkey builder for both standalone metal-roofing projects and complete new builds.

The company emphasizes its family-owned status, licensed and insured standing, and a focus on seamless communication from project start to finish as key differentiators. It also highlights affordable pricing and the convenience of a single contractor handling everything from dirt work to final roofing.

name: Baycable
old_description: BAYCABLE is the one source for custom cable assembly solutions. We have the resources, innovative technology and industry expertise to meet the growing needs of customers around the corner and around the world.
about:
Baycable operates from Fremont, California, where it has served the interconnect market for over 50 years. The privately held company traces its roots to a focus on custom cable assembly solutions and has grown to maintain two ISO-registered facilities in North America.

The company designs and manufactures electro-mechanical assemblies, molded cable assemblies, coil cords, and specialty cable. Its capabilities span custom cable assembly, coil cord production, and molding, supported by an in-house machine shop that produces mold tools and custom components. Certified IPC-620 trainers work on the floor, and production runs range from prototype through medium volume.

Baycable supplies OEMs, ODMs, and their contractors across medical, industrial, automotive, audio, and semiconductor sectors. Examples cited include medical RF generator cables and automotive coil cords for defrost functions.

The firm emphasizes its in-house engineering team—compound, process, and electronic engineers—as a differentiator, enabling application-specific solutions for complex interconnection problems. UL and CSA approvals are available, and the company holds ISO 9001:2015, ISO 13485:2016, and IATF 16949 certifications.

The firm provides solar energy system installation and consulting services for residential customers. Its offerings include free on-site evaluations to assess solar needs, assistance with the 30% federal tax credit, and procurement of equipment from major solar technology suppliers. The company does not manufacture its own panels or hardware but integrates systems from providers. No details on facility size, headcount, or annual volumes are publicly disclosed.

Bayou Solar serves the renewable energy and solar energy industries, primarily targeting homeowners with electric, gas, or propane water heaters and properties with pools. The company’s consultation process gathers details about existing hot water systems and pool ownership to tailor solar solutions for energy cost reduction.

The business emphasizes its state licensing and access to federal incentives as key differentiators for customers seeking to reduce energy costs through solar adoption. It positions itself as a local contractor that manages the full evaluation and incentive process.
